findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every request, not only when optimized_pagination=true, so any caller with no membership row (active staff without the superuser flag, legacy org ApiKey or sentry-app proxy users where request.user is not a member) gets AttributeError on None and every audit-log GET returns 500

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key runs math.floor/math.ceil on the `datetime` attribute (a datetime object), which raises TypeError. build_cursor calls it for any non-empty page, so the opt-in path returns 500 whenever there is at least one audit row

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The "negative offset" path slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start (e.g. cursor `0:-5:1` or `0:-100:0`), and Django rejects that with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). paginate() does not map that to 400 because it only catches BadPaginationError, so the "ORM handles negative slicing" and "safe" comments are false and the advertised feature can never work

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Shared BasePaginator (Paginator/DateTimePaginator, used by many endpoints) now handles negative offsets inconsistently. Next cursors are silently clamped to 0, which masks bad input: has_prev is forced true via bool(offset), and next_offset is built from the raw negative offset, which can repeat pages. Prev cursors (`X:-5:1`) still reach QuerySet slicing and return 500. OffsetPaginator (line 286) raises BadPaginationError instead

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (a ms-epoch int from DateTimePaginator Link headers), so build_queryset emits `datetime <= <integer>`. Postgres rejects that timestamptz/integer comparison, so reusing an existing cursor with optimized_pagination=true fails with a DB error. Cursors are not interchangeable between the two paginators, despite the claimed "backward compatibility"

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod were removed from the serializer, and DRF silently ignores unknown query params, so existing clients sending a date window get unfiltered full history with 200 and no error. src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The "authorized administrators" gate checks the raw `request.user.is_superuser` DB flag instead of an active superuser session (is_active_superuser), and has_global_access is an org open-membership/global-role flag, not an admin check, so the gate does not match its comment

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — The stated performance purpose is not delivered. src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The "negative offset" path slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start (e.g. cursor `0:-5:1` or `0:-100:0`), and Django rejects that with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). paginate() does not map that to 400 because it only catches BadPaginationError, so the "ORM handles negative slicing" and "safe" comments are false and the advertised feature can never work

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Shared BasePaginator (Paginator/DateTimePaginator, used by many endpoints) now handles negative offsets inconsistently. Next cursors are silently clamped to 0, which masks bad input: has_prev is forced true via bool(offset), and next_offset is built from the raw negative offset, which can repeat pages. Prev cursors (`X:-5:1`) still reach QuerySet slicing and return 500. OffsetPaginator (line 286) raises BadPaginationError instead

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the diff changes slicing to clamp `start_offset = max(0, offset)` only when `not cursor.is_prev`, but leaves `cursor.is_prev` using the raw `offset` (`start_offset = offset`). That means negative offsets are now handled inconsistently depending on direction: forward pagination silently clamps to 0 while reverse pagination can still pass a negative start into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The raw `offset` is also still used later in the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check, so a negative `offset` can skew cursor/page trimming logic. Separately, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` explicitly allows negative slicing (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `< 0`), which is a fragile/broken assumption for Django QuerySet slicing and can error. These behaviors align with the finding that negative offsets can lead to repeated/incorrect pagination or errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (a ms-epoch int from DateTimePaginator Link headers), so build_queryset emits `datetime <= <integer>`. Postgres rejects that timestamptz/integer comparison, so reusing an existing cursor with optimized_pagination=true fails with a DB error. Cursors are not interchangeable between the two paginators, despite the claimed "backward compatibility"

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to the new OptimizedCursorPaginator when `optimized_pagination=true`, but still paginates on `order_by="-datetime"` (i.e., a datetime/timestamptz key). In OptimizedCursorPaginator, `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged and `get_item_key` applies `math.floor/ceil` to `getattr(item, self.key)`, which strongly implies it expects a numeric key/cursor value, not a datetime. If an existing cursor produced by DateTimePaginator encodes the datetime as an integer (as the finding states), OptimizedCursorPaginator will pass that integer into `build_queryset(...)` for a datetime field, leading to an invalid datetime-vs-integer comparison in the DB and breaking cursor interoperability when toggling `optimized_pagination`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — start/end/statsPeriod were removed from the serializer, and DRF silently ignores unknown query params, so existing clients sending a date window get unfiltered full history with 200 and no error. This is a silent pass that also works against the PR's performance goal by removing the scan bound

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any removal of `start`, `end`, or `statsPeriod` from a serializer (or any serializer changes at all). The only changes in `organization_auditlogs.py` are around choosing between `DateTimePaginator` and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on `optimized_pagination` and admin access, plus paginator/cursor offset logic. Therefore the claim about DRF silently ignoring unknown date-window params and returning unfiltered full history is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The "authorized administrators" gate checks the raw `request.user.is_superuser` DB flag instead of an active superuser session (is_active_superuser), and has_global_access is an org open-membership/global-role flag, not an admin check, so the gate does not match its comment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an "authorized administrators" gate in `organization_auditlogs.py` using `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. From the diff alone, it’s verifiable that the comment/intent (“authorized administrators”) is not clearly aligned with the chosen flags (one is a raw DB superuser boolean; the other is named “global access” rather than “admin”), which is a concrete review concern about permission semantics and clarity. However, the claim that it must use `is_active_superuser` (and that `has_global_access` is definitively not an admin check) cannot be confirmed from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73 — The stated performance purpose is not delivered. Apart from the added negative-offset branch, the opt-in paginator runs the same SQL as DateTimePaginator and still has no max_offset, so huge cursors like `0:1000000000:0` still force deep OFFSET scans. The only new behavior is an "access beyond normal pagination bounds" branch that looks like a disguised capability, not an optimization

adjudication.rationale: The diff-backed behavior supports the review concern that the “optimized” path doesn’t obviously avoid deep OFFSET scans: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result()` still slices the Django queryset (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`), which is implemented as LIMIT/OFFSET, and there is no max-offset cap introduced anywhere in this diff. The only clearly new behavior is allowing negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is true (`start_offset = cursor.offset` when `< 0`), which changes capabilities/semantics rather than providing a verifiable performance improvement from the diff alone. The claim that it runs the *same SQL as DateTimePaginator* isn’t strictly provable from the diff, but the core point (no demonstrated offset-scan avoidance and no offset limiting) is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs on every request, even without `optimized_pagination`, and `member` can be None for non-member callers (API-key auth, staff), so existing audit-log GETs now return 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, so `organization_context.member.has_global_access` may be dereferenced even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested. The diff does not show that `organization_context.member` is always non-None for this endpoint, so an AttributeError is a plausible edge case introduced by this change, but the claim that it will definitely 500 for non-member callers is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:24 — Removing the `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` serializer fields makes DRF silently drop them, so existing callers that filter by date now get the full unfiltered audit history with a 200 instead of filtered results (or a 400 for bad input).

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes pagination behavior in `organization_auditlogs.py` (adding an `optimized_pagination` flag and selecting `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator`) and adds a new paginator plus offset handling changes. There is no shown change removing `start`/`end`/`statsPeriod` from any serializer or request parsing, so the finding about DRF silently dropping those fields and returning unfiltered audit history is not supported by the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the `datetime` field, so any non-empty `optimized_pagination=true` response raises TypeError (500) while building its Link cursors.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new optimized path paginates audit logs ordered by `-datetime` using `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`. The added `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on that value and casts to `int`. If `self.key` corresponds to the datetime field used for ordering (as implied by `order_by="-datetime"`), `value` will be a `datetime`, and `math.floor/ceil(datetime)` will raise `TypeError`, breaking cursor construction for any `optimized_pagination=true` request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer instead of converting DateTimePaginator's millisecond-epoch cursor, so Link-header cursors are not interchangeable between the two paginators on the same endpoint and get compared as ints against a datetime column.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and uses it on the audit logs endpoint with `order_by="-datetime"` (a datetime field). In `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged, and `get_item_key` applies `math.floor/ceil` to `getattr(item, self.key)`. With a datetime key, this will not match DateTimePaginator semantics (which typically normalize/convert datetimes for cursor comparisons) and makes cursors generated by one paginator not safely reusable with the other on the same endpoint. This can lead to incorrect filtering/comparisons against a datetime column and potentially runtime type errors or broken pagination when switching modes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The advertised negative-offset cursor contract cannot work: slicing a Django QuerySet with a negative start raises "Negative indexing is not supported", so negative cursors return a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces/permits negative offsets and then slices Django querysets with a negative start index. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Additionally, the modified existing paginator logic sets `start_offset = offset` whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true, which also allows negative offsets to reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexing, so this can raise and produce a 500 for negative cursors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — The new `optimized_pagination` query param is not declared in AuditLogQueryParamSerializer or the API docs, and non-admins silently fall back to the old paginator, so the same request gets different cursor semantics depending on the caller's role with nothing telling them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `optimized_pagination` query param check in `organization_auditlogs.py` (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and gates the new paginator behind `enable_advanced` (superuser or `organization_context.member.has_global_access`). This means the same request with `optimized_pagination=true` will produce different pagination/cursor behavior depending on caller role, and non-admins silently fall back to `DateTimePaginator` with no indication in the response. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — This shared BasePaginator change affects every paginated endpoint, not just audit logs: negative next-cursor offsets now silently clamp to 0 instead of erroring, while negative prev-cursor offsets still fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:842 — value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which build_queryset compares against the datetime column; no test follows a next/prev cursor through the optimized paginator.

The diff also shows no accompanying tests for next/prev cursor behavior, but the type/key mismatch is itself a concrete behavioral defect introduced by wiring this paginator into an endpoint ordered by a datetime field.
